body:
Added examples for training hyperparameters with EKP and the current interfaces. Minimizes a cost that approximates the KRR cost function (i.e. misfit + RKHS norm) weighted by noise and variability from data and random features.

Further work could look at optimizing randomized Kernel-flow cost functions

## Content
1. `_direct` approximates the kernel ridge regression function with misfit weighted by `noise_sd^2`
2. `_withcov` as in `_direct`, but the weights the misfit with the RF posterior variance. Performs better in >1D
3. `_matchingcov` as in `_withcov` but also tries to nudge the RF posterior variance towards `noise_sd^2`. 
These are used in `test/Methods/runtests/jl` to obtain reasonable lengthscales.

## Example results
- `1d_to_1d_regression_direct_matchingcov.jl` - 1d input - 1d output problem, learning a standard deviation of the centred Gaussian feature distribution for three Random feature types (Fourier, Relu & Sigmoid) here with 80 data points
[Fit_and_predict_1D_4.pdf](https://github.com/CliMA/RandomFeatures.jl/files/9629436/Fit_and_predict_1D.pdf)
- `nd_to_1d_regression_direct_matchingcov.jl` - nd input  - 1d output problem with Fourier features, and 1 standard deviation of a Gaussian learnt per dimension.  e.g. 40 data points in 1D and for 6D (tested to work ok up-to 10D) [NB i think I used more points to predict here, in the final graphs so the uncertainties are reduced compared with below]
